report.title: Payments v2.4.0 shrank the DB connection pool from 50 to 5, causing 502s from checkout and api-gateway
report.summary: Since 11:31Z, payments has been returning 503 because it can't get a DB connection from its pool. Deploy v2.4.0 at 11:29Z ("Refactor DB client config loading", commit 9f3c2ab) dropped pool.max_size from 50 to 5. Checkout passes the failures on as 502s, and api-gateway is at 7.5–32.5% 5xx with p95 latency around 4.3–4.8s. Mitigation: roll payments back to v2.3.0.
report.impact: Since 2026-10-21T11:32Z, 7.5–32.5% of api-gateway requests per minute fail with 5xx (32.5% in the last full minute, 11:38Z, and the trend is up). p95 latency went from about 180ms to about 4.5s. Gateway volume is about 1000 req/min. All gateway traffic goes to checkout, so order building and submission are affected: checkout errors are 7.5–20%, and payments errors are 12.5–25% since 11:31Z. Inventory is not affected.

root_cause.hypothesis: Payments v2.4.0 refactored how the DB client loads its config. The new version starts with pool.max_size=5 instead of the previous 50. The pool is pinned at 5/5, so requests wait 3000ms for a connection and fail with 503. Checkout reports those as 502, and so does api-gateway.
root_cause.trigger: Deploy of payments v2.3.0 -> v2.4.0 at 2026-10-21T11:29:00Z by ci-bot, commit 9f3c2ab, "Refactor DB client config loading"

evidence.finding: api-gateway (v1.12.3, no version change): error rate was 0 from 11:04 to 11:31Z, apart from 2.5% at 11:03. It then went to 22.5% at 11:32, between 7.5% and 25% through 11:37, and 32.5% at 11:38. p95 latency rose from about 170–190ms to 4310–4839ms. Volume held steady at 1000 req/min.
api-gateway ERROR logs, 11:00–11:39Z: 53 errors. 52 of them are "upstream checkout returned 502 Bad Gateway" and 1 is a generic 500. They come from all 3 gateway hosts.
api-gateway depends only on checkout. Checkout depends on payments and inventory. Payments depends on postgres.
checkout (v3.8.0, no version change): error rate 0 through 11:31Z, then 7.5–20% from 11:32Z. p95 latency went from about 150ms to 4308–4700ms.
checkout ERROR logs: 43 errors. 39 of them are "upstream payments returned 503 Service Unavailable" (returned to the gateway as 502), and 4 are generic 500s.

payments: on v2.3.0 until 11:28Z, db_pool_max was 50 and db_pool_active 18, with errors near 0. From 11:29Z on v2.4.0, db_pool_max=5 and db_pool_active=5, so the pool is fully used. Errors went to 25% at 11:31Z and stayed between 12.5% and 25%. p95 latency rose from about 120ms to 4043–4336ms.
payments logs, 11:20–11:39Z: 67 lines of "TimeoutError: could not acquire connection from pool (max_size=5, timeout=3000ms)", all status 503. The other 692 requests returned 200.
Startup line from payments v2.4.0 at 2026-10-21T11:29:20Z on payments-1: "db client initialized: pool.max_size=5 pool.timeout_ms=3000".
Only one deploy between 11:00 and 11:39Z: payments v2.3.0 -> v2.4.0 at 11:29:00Z, commit 9f3c2ab, "Refactor DB client config loading", status succeeded.

inventory (v1.4.2) is healthy: error rate 0–2.5% (one 500 at 11:36Z) and p95 latency 56–64ms, with no change over the window. postgres returned no metrics, so the database side is not directly verified.

timeline.event: Last minute on payments v2.3.0: db_pool_max=50, db_pool_active=18, error rate 0.
payments v2.4.0 deployed (commit 9f3c2ab, "Refactor DB client config loading"). db_pool_max drops to 5.
payments-1 logs "db client initialized: pool.max_size=5 pool.timeout_ms=3000".
payments pool is full (5/5). Error rate hits 25% with connection-pool timeouts (503), and p95 reaches 4149ms.
checkout errors reach 15% (payments 503 passed on as 502). api-gateway errors reach 22.5%, with p95 at 4533ms.
Datadog alert fires: api-gateway 5xx at 18.4% over 5 minutes, threshold 5%.
api-gateway error rate reaches 32.5%, the highest so far.

next_steps: Roll payments back from v2.4.0 to v2.3.0 now. Don't wait for a fix-forward.

Check recovery within about 5 minutes: payments db_pool_max back to 50, the pool-timeout errors stop, and payments, checkout and api-gateway 5xx return to near 0 with p95 back to roughly 120ms, 150ms and 180ms.

Post in the incident channel: about 1 in 4 requests to api-gateway/checkout are failing since 11:32Z because of the payments v2.4.0 pool regression, and a rollback is in progress. Update every 15 minutes.
Ask data-platform to check postgres connection and load health. No postgres metrics were available during this investigation.

Open a ticket for the payments team with the deploy, first errors, error message and config diff (pool.max_size 50 -> 5). Commit 9f3c2ab probably lost the pool-size override and fell back to a default of 5.
Add an alert on db_pool_active/db_pool_max saturation for payments, and a pre-deploy check that compares the pool config between versions.

report.title: api-gateway 5xx (7.5–32.5%) caused by payments v2.4.0 shrinking its DB connection pool from 50 to 5
report.summary: Since about 11:32 UTC, api-gateway has returned 502s on 7.5–32.5% of requests, and p95 latency is around 4.5s. The errors pass up the chain payments → checkout → api-gateway. They start in payments v2.4.0, deployed at 11:29 UTC (commit 9f3c2ab, 'Refactor DB client config loading'). That deploy set the DB pool to max_size=5 (it was 50), so requests now time out waiting for a connection. Rolling payments back to v2.3.0 is the immediate fix.
report.impact: From 11:32 UTC to now, 7.5–32.5% of public API requests through api-gateway have failed with 502 (32.5% in the 11:38 minute, and rising), and gateway p95 latency went from about 185ms to 4.3–4.8s. The failures affect the checkout/order path: checkout errors are 7.5–20% and payments errors are 12.5–25%. Payment authorize and capture requests are failing, so some orders cannot be placed. Most requests still succeed.

root_cause.hypothesis: The DB client config refactor in payments v2.4.0 starts with pool.max_size=5 instead of 50. All 5 connections are in use (db_pool_active=5/5), so requests wait 3000ms, time out with 'could not acquire connection from pool' and return 503. checkout turns these into 502s, and api-gateway passes the 502s on to users.
root_cause.trigger: payments deploy v2.3.0 → v2.4.0 at 2026-10-21T11:29:00Z (commit 9f3c2ab, ci-bot, 'Refactor DB client config loading')
